purpose: Evaluate the same observable score-preserving path near the data's low-label estimation boundary using a finite ridge anchor. This is a distinct follow-up after the original 50-label path showed no exterior moment in its first 260 retained allocations; the complete original 500-allocation result remains required and will be reported.
allocation: Original 240 five-row block permutation; blocks are the released source convention and not verified participant identifiers
anchor: Human ridge logit minimizing labelled mean loss + ||beta||^2/(2*m), on all 11 coefficients, using only the same 20 labelled rows
anchor_penalty: 1/m; fixed before this follow-up, matching the already-used ridge scale in the paper's finite-support comparator
base_power: Existing pooled-information scalar variance rule at the fixed ridge anchor; retain zero, one and unresolved values explicitly
path: lambda_t=alpha+t*(1-alpha); g_t=mu_anchor+(alpha/lambda_t)*(g-mu_anchor) for positive lambda_t; exact zero uses ordinary human logit
nuisance_fallbacks: Retain all prior fallbacks from the original nuisance function at this smaller budget; do not delete any allocation
endpoints: Separate alpha=0, alpha=1 and 0<alpha<1. Positive powers when alpha=0 have zero surrogate-score variance and do not count as defined recomputed variance optima.
interpretation: Allocation-conditional descriptive availability diagnostic. No new estimator recommendation, optimality, inference coverage, independent test sample or Gaussian phase validation.
